thread.query: Lenovo Legion monitor HDR brightness drops

posts.subject: Brightness slider and keyboard shortcuts don’t change brightness on Lenovo LOQ
posts.author: Sarker_Shuvo
posts.message_html:
Hi everyone,

I have a Lenovo LOQ (machine type/model 83JE0110AD). The brightness controls aren’t changing the built-in screen brightness:

The Windows brightness slider moves, but the screen stays at the same brightness.
The keyboard brightness shortcuts don’t work.
Device Manager shows Intel UHD Graphics, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5050 Laptop GPU, and Integrated Monitor.
HDR is off.
Lenovo Vantage doesn’t show an Intel graphics update. The available BIOS update is R3CN44WW; my current BIOS is R3CN39WW.
I’m trying the monitor-device reinstall by uninstalling Integrated Monitor in Device Manager and restarting. If that doesn’t help, what should I try next? Could this be related to the Intel graphics driver, BIOS, or display hardware?

Thanks!

posts.subject: Re:Brightness slider and keyboard shortcuts don’t change brightness on Lenovo LOQ
posts.author: Hassen_Lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hello Sarker_Shuvo,

If reinstalling the Integrated Monitor does not help, the next things to check would be the display and graphics drivers.

  1. In Device Manager, try uninstalling the Intel UHD Graphics driver (check Delete the driver software for this device if available), then restart and install the Intel graphics driver provided for your model from the Lenovo support page. Brightness control on the internal display is typically handled through the integrated graphics driver, so a driver issue can cause the slider to move without any actual brightness change.

  2. Since you are currently on BIOS R3CN39WW and a newer R3CN44WW version is available, it may also be worth updating the BIOS. BIOS updates can include fixes related to hardware control and device compatibility.

  3. If the issue persists, boot into the BIOS setup and check whether the display appears to remain at a fixed brightness there as well. If brightness cannot be adjusted even outside of Windows, that could help determine whether the issue is software-related or related to the display hardware/firmware.

  4. You can also test whether the problem occurs in Safe Mode. If brightness control works there, it would further point toward a driver or software conflict in Windows.

Just to confirm, did the brightness controls work normally when the system was new, or did the issue start after a Windows update, driver update, or BIOS update? Also, are you using the original Lenovo graphics drivers or drivers installed directly from Intel/NVIDIA?

Best regards,
Hassen_Lenovo
